items.feedback: Right: the loop of choose action, run it, feed the result back is what makes it an agent; a longer prompt or bigger model only changes what one call can do.

You assumed the model reaches into the booking system itself. It can't: it only writes text. Its output is a structured request naming check_calendar with the machine and date as arguments, and the program around it runs the tool. The answer looks looked-up, but the program did the lookup.
Right: repeating the same failure needs a stopping condition, and a step limit supplies one; a bigger window or stronger prompt doesn't end a loop.
Same M4 as q2: the program runs the tools, not the model. Count one model call per input it receives: the question plus 3 tool results = 4 calls.
You have what happens: the result goes back to the model. The missing part is why: it goes into the model's next input so the model can use it to pick its next step or write the final answer.

Right that the model is given each tool's name and description and picks the fit. Wrong that it remembers past choices on its own: chatbots seem to remember because the program re-sends history. The model keeps nothing between sessions; its choice comes from the descriptions alone.

summary: You have the loop's shape and the role of tool descriptions, but you gave the model program-side jobs: running tools (q2, q4) and storing memory (q6). Work on separating what the model does (writes text) from what the program does (runs tools, stores and supplies memory). Next, retrace one request on paper, labelling each step 'model' or 'program', before the context and memory lesson.
